subtitulo: Purpose, length and where you sleep — short, true, and backed by the booking you saved last night
cena: The officer's eyes are already moving to the next person in the queue, and the only thing between you and the stamp is three short sentences.
frasePiso: Answer the question that was asked. The booking carries everything else.

steps.pt: Passport control is not an Italian exam. Three jobs only: why you came, how long, where you sleep. True answer, then stop.

steps.es: Buongiorno. Qual è il motivo del viaggio?
steps.pt: Good morning. What is the purpose of your trip?
steps.tts: Buongiorno. Qual è il motivo del viaggio?
steps.acao: Answer only the purpose. Do not add the itinerary.

steps.promptPt: You are travelling for a holiday. One sentence. Speak now.

steps.pt: Use your real number. Ten days is the rehearsal value, not a line to memorise for every trip.

steps.promptPt: Give only the duration, nothing else. Speak now.

steps.acao: Name the city and the accommodation type. Nothing else.

steps.pt: Not the story of how you found the hotel. Name it, and let the booking you saved hold the address.

steps.promptPt: Say where you are staying, briefly. Speak now.
Hand over the offline confirmation without adding a speech. Speak now.

steps.pt: Eccola is the whole sentence. Two syllables and an outstretched hand beat a paragraph every time.

steps.promptPt: You did not catch the question. Ask cleanly, without apologising twice. Speak now.
steps.es: Scusi, non ho capito la domanda.
steps.pinyin: SKOO-zee, non oh ka-PEE-to la do-MAN-da
steps.pt: Sorry, I didn't understand the question.
steps.tts: Scusi, non ho capito la domanda.

steps.promptPt: Say you are travelling alone. Speak now.
They ask if you are visiting other cities. Answer briefly and truthfully. Speak now.

steps.pt: All right. Have a good trip.

steps.promptPt: Close it in two words and move on. Speak now.

steps.es: Sono in vacanza. Dieci giorni. In un hotel a Roma. Sì, eccola.
steps.pinyin: SO-no een va-KAN-tsa. dee-EH-chee JOR-nee. een oon o-TEL a RO-ma. see, EK-ko-la
steps.pt: Shadow the three answers with a clean stop after each.
steps.tts: Sono in vacanza. Dieci giorni. In un hotel a Roma. Sì, eccola.

steps.pt: B05 done. Purpose, duration, where you sleep. Short is not evasive — short means the answer matched the question.

aprofundar.titulo: The border is a matching task

secoes.corpo: Never repeat the lesson's ten days when your itinerary says something else. Replace the number with the truth; the structure stays exactly as short.
Purpose, duration and accommodation are three separate answers. Do not stack all three unless you were asked for them together — the officer is working through a queue of matched pairs.
Eccola moves the exchange from your memory to your evidence. It is the shortest useful sentence in the whole course and it does more work than any explanation.

secoes.titulo: Rules move, so check before you fly
secoes.corpo: Entry requirements for non-EU travellers to the Schengen area have been changing, including new electronic entry systems phased in across borders. This part teaches the conversation, not the paperwork — verify the current requirement with an official source close to departure.

permissao: You are allowed to answer in three words and stop. A short true answer is not suspicious — over-explaining, filling silence with unasked detail or trying to sound friendlier than the question calls for is what actually slows a border desk down.
espelho: Anyone who has over-answered a customs officer at home by volunteering details nobody wanted knows the instinct this part corrects. It is not an Italian problem — it is the nervous habit of filling silence with more words than the question needs, and it reads the same on either side of any border.

fichasCulturais.sinal: The officer asks one short question and you find yourself adding an explanation nobody requested — why this trip, what you did last time, how excited you are.
fichasCulturais.suaLeitura: More detail sounds friendlier, and proves I have nothing to hide.
fichasCulturais.oQueEAli: The desk is processing a queue of short matched answers. A reply that runs past the question it answered reads as something to double-check, not as warmth.
fichasCulturais.oQueVoceFaz: Answer only the payload of the question you were just asked, then stop and wait for the next one.
fichasCulturais.oQueMelhora: The exchange moves at the pace the officer is already set up for, and you are through faster rather than slower.
fichasCulturais.ondeNaoVale: Not when the officer asks a compound question or explicitly invites more detail — then answering everything they actually asked is the match, and a clipped reply would be the mismatch.
